digest: Found polling defaults/clamping, stop-error classification, cancellation overclassification, and a dispose race risk.

findings.title: Polling default and minimum violate S3
findings.evidence: pollMs defaults to 200ms and is clamped to 1ms, while the specification requires a 50ms default and a 10ms minimum.
evidenceQuotes: **S3.** 중지 감시 주기(`pollMs`)의 기본값은 50ms이고, 호출자가 더 작은 값을 주어도 10ms보다
findings.rationale: Stop detection can be four times slower than the contract by default, and callers can request a 1ms interval, causing excessive polling and violating the stated lower bound.
findings.recommendedAction: Use a 50ms fallback and clamp with Math.max(10, ...), including appropriate handling for invalid numeric inputs.

findings.title: Stop-error classifier accepts message text instead of name only
findings.evidence: The classifier returns true when an Error message merely starts with the stop-request prefix, regardless of its error name.
findings.rationale: S6 requires recognition only when the error name is WorkflowStopRequested. Message-based matching can misclassify unrelated provider or application errors as workflow stops and suppress diagnostics.
findings.recommendedAction: Remove the message-prefix condition and require error.name === WORKFLOW_STOP_REQUESTED_ERROR_NAME.

findings.title: Cancellation classifier promotes non-contract provider markers
findings.evidence: The implementation treats cancelled booleans and the strings cancelled and timeout as cancellation, while C1 permits only aborted, AbortError, and ABORT_ERR for error/reason strings.
evidenceQuotes: if (candidate === "aborted" || candidate === "AbortError" || candidate === "ABORT_ERR" || candidate === "cancelled" || candidate === "timeout") return true;
findings.rationale: A provider error or timeout represented by these extra markers can be promoted to workflow cancellation, violating the exact classification contract and potentially suppressing real failures.
findings.recommendedAction: Restrict error/reason string matching to the three specified values and confirm whether boolean cancelled fields are explicitly part of the provider contract before retaining them.

findings.title: dispose has no lifecycle fence for an already-queued polling callback
findings.evidence: dispose only clears the interval; the polling callback and check function have no disposed state check before invoking readWorkflowStopIntent.
evidenceQuotes: const timer = setInterval(() => void check(), pollMs);
findings.rationale: If an interval callback has already been queued when dispose runs, clearing the timer alone does not fence that callback from entering check and starting a new disk read, conflicting with S5. The async read also remains active after disposal.
findings.recommendedAction: Track a disposed boolean, set it before clearing the timer, and check it at the start of check (and before any subsequent polling work).

sourceCoverage.evidence: if (candidate === "aborted" || candidate === "AbortError" || candidate === "ABORT_ERR" || candidate === "cancelled" || candidate === "timeout") return true;
**S3.** 중지 감시 주기(`pollMs`)의 기본값은 50ms이고, 호출자가 더 작은 값을 주어도 10ms보다

noIssueNotes: S4 is satisfied: the monitoring path catches read failures, while throwIfWorkflowStopRequested propagates them.
S1, S2, S7, and C2 have no additional defect evident in the inspected ranges.
